threads.body: [Testing] The interceptor producer-span test in `AbstractInterceptorsTest` validates this span's shape but never compares its start and end timestamps, so the zero-duration requirement can regress unnoticed. Add an assertion that `getEndEpochNanos()` equals `getStartEpochNanos()`, following the existing SQS synthetic-span test pattern.

replies.body: I’m intentionally not asserting zero duration here. Unlike synthetic `create` spans, this span represents an operation that ideally includes network duration. It is zero-duration only because the interceptor API does not expose hooks around the operation, so encoding that limitation in the test would prevent a future instrumentation improvement.

threads.body: Using `Instant.now()` introduces reliance on wall-clock time (which can jump due to NTP/clock adjustments) for span timestamps. Since you only need a “now” value to create a zero-duration span, it’d be more robust to use a shared/SDK-consistent time source (e.g., an OpenTelemetry clock/time utility used elsewhere in this instrumentation) so timestamps align with other spans produced by the same library and are less sensitive to wall-clock corrections.

`InstrumenterUtil.startAndEnd(...)` ends the span before header propagation runs. If `KafkaPropagation.propagateContext(...)` throws (or otherwise fails), that failure can no longer be recorded on the span, whereas previously the `end(...)` happened in a `finally` and could observe the thrown error. Consider switching back to a `try/finally` structure where you end the span after propagation, but still force zero-duration by using the same explicit timestamp for start/end and passing any thrown `Throwable` into `end(...)` (or using an `InstrumenterUtil` helper that supports explicit timestamps + error propagation).

This test updates the call signature but doesn’t assert the new behavior that motivated the change (that interceptor-created spans are zero-duration). Add an assertion that the produced receive span has `startTime == endTime` (or duration == 0) to prevent regressions back to measurable interceptor execution time.
